title: Security appliances software versions MX 26.1.5 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Generally Available MX Security & SD-WAN firmware is now available

Executive summary: MX 26.1.5 is a maintenance update for the MX 26.1 Generally Available release family.
This release adds support for C8111-C-G2-MX, C8121-W-G2-MX, and C8121-CW-G2-MX secure routers.
This release includes fixes for AutoVPN, Client VPN, Cisco Secure Client, routing, SNMP, syslog, Mandatory DHCP, AMP stability, and Local Status Page behavior.
This release also includes platform-specific fixes for C8455-G2-MX, MX95, MX105, MX67, MX68, and Z4 devices.
What's new: Added support for C8111-C-G2-MX, C8121-W-G2-MX, and C8121-CW-G2-MX secure routers.
Bug fixes - general fixes: Corrected an issue that could prevent group policies from applying reliably to Client VPN and Cisco Secure Client VPN users when a VPN user reconnected with a different assigned VPN IP address. (MX-46090, MX-46136)
Resolved a rare issue that could prevent new Cisco Secure Client VPN sessions from being established. (MX-40793)
Fixed a rare issue that could cause device instability when AMP was enabled. (MX-48940)
Resolved an issue that could cause unexpected warm spare failover events during periods of high-bandwidth client traffic. (MX-43047)
Resolved an issue that could cause WAN failover to take longer than expected and disrupt AutoVPN tunnels in specific MX networks. (MX-47742)

Corrected an issue with IP spoofing protection on MX 26.1. In networks with certain static routes, traffic with spoofed source IP addresses could pass through the MX instead of being dropped. This could occur when the spoofed source IP fell within a static route whose next hop was in a different VLAN. (MX-42527)
Resolved an issue that could disrupt traffic using LAN static routes after VLAN route updates. (MX-46754)
Fixed an issue that could cause Mandatory DHCP to drop traffic from clients with valid DHCP leases after an MX appliance rebooted, upgraded, or took over as a warm spare. (MX-48417)

Resolved an issue that could fragment NetFlow and syslog traffic sent through VPN tunnels. This could add reassembly load on concentrator MX appliances when many spokes sent telemetry to collectors behind a hub. (MX-46114)
Corrected an issue that could cause syslog failover and failback messages to identify the previous WAN uplink instead of the newly selected uplink. (MX-45754)

Resolved an issue that could prevent LAN clients from reaching the Local Status Page after an MX appliance was factory reset while offline, until the appliance connected to Dashboard and downloaded its configuration. (MX-47727)
Bug fixes - limited platform fixes: Resolved a performance issue that could delay VLAN configuration on C8455-G2-MX appliances when large VLAN sets were configured. (MX-45408)
Resolved an issue that could cause C8455-G2-MX appliances to forward CDP or LLDP packets between LAN ports. (MX-44416)
Resolved an issue that could prevent SNMP IF-MIB data from being returned on MX75, MX85, MX95, and MX105 appliances running MX 26.1. (MX-46357)
Resolved an issue that could prevent MX95 and MX105 SFP uplinks from establishing link when the connected peer forced 1 Gbps full duplex. (MX-23147)
Resolved an issue on MX95 and MX105 appliances that could cause traffic for a previously native VLAN to leave a LAN trunk port untagged after the port was changed to drop untagged traffic. (MX-43150)

Corrected an issue that could cause MX250 and MX450 appliances to show the first two WAN interfaces as Internet and Port 2 instead of Internet 1 and Internet 2 on the Local Status Page Configure page. (MX-46828)
Resolved an issue that could prevent cellular-only MX appliances from establishing AutoVPN tunnels after upgrading to MX 26.1 or later. (MX-47302)
Resolved an issue that could reduce AutoVPN TCP throughput on MX67, MX68, MX75, MX85, and Z-series appliances over higher-latency VPN paths. (MX-48759)
Resolved an issue that could prevent MX67C and MX68CW appliances from detecting an installed working SIM. (MX-47134)
Corrected an issue that could cause wired clients to appear as associated wireless clients on wireless-capable MX and Z appliances. (MX-41960)
Resolved an issue on Z4 appliances where clients on LAN ports using hybrid authentication could fail to reconnect after an appliance reboot until the client or port was reconnected. (MX-44580)
Resolved an issue that could cause MX67, MX67C, MX67W, MX68, MX68W, and MX68CW appliances to restart unexpectedly. (HWMX-242)
Fixed an issue that could prevent 10G copper SFP+ modules from establishing link after reboot on C8455-G2-MX appliances. (MX-49415)
Resolved a performance regression that could reduce wired throughput on MX68 appliances after upgrading to MX 26.1. (MX-49693)
Legacy products notice: When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.
When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.
Other: The product complies with EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2: 2024
Added the cellular IP address to the Local Status Page.
Clarified the wording for the Cellular Override options in the Local Status Page. (MX-29835)
